title: 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup

epigraph.quote: Individual stock strength must always be weighed against market weather; in a ten-distribution-day downtrend with failing asymmetry, discipline means stepping aside.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein Tape Discipline

web_blocks.html: The broader U.S. equity market weakened sharply in late November. On November 20, 2026, the S&P 500 sat in a confirmed Downtrend. Only 38.8% of benchmark stocks traded above their 50-day SMA, and 46.9% held above their 200-day SMA. Just 3 of 11 sectors held above their 50-day averages alongside 10 distribution days in 25 sessions. Against that weak backdrop, Chubb closed at $371.63 (+0.41% 1D), preserving its primary Stage 2 uptrend while showing early internal distribution.

Both quantitative ledgers agree on trend stage with zero divergence. The daily `facts` ledger tags CB as Stage 2 (Markup) (`stage: 2`), and the TradingView snapshot tags CB as STAGE_2 (`CLEAR_FOR_CONSIDERATION`). Price sits +0.97% above its 20-day SMA ($368.06) and +3.58% above its 10-week EMA ($358.80; `facts` $357.83). Shares also hold +5.44% (+2.86 ATRs) above the rising 50-day SMA ($352.46), +8.32% above the 30-week SMA ($343.09), and +9.70% above the 200-day SMA ($338.77). Minor window differences exist between feeds: `facts` and Finviz show -1.09% 1W, +2.11% 1M, +7.46% 3M returns, and 1.47x 20D relative volume, while TradingView shows -0.98% 1W, +4.24% 1M, +8.15% 3M, and 1.43x 30D relative volume.

web_blocks.html: Multi-timeframe inspection from the November 20 chart feed reveals real near-term friction beneath the Stage 2 headline. On the 4-hour chart, CB sits right beneath its 4H 20-EMA ($371.81) with a neutral 4H RSI of 51.79 and `intraday_4h_turn: false`, while 4H 50-SMA support rests at $366.14. Over the past 25 sessions, CB also logged 5 stock distribution days on 1.47x 20D relative volume (2.25M shares on Nov 20), showing institutional supply into rallies even with 7.20% Bollinger bandwidth.

Even though the automated Stage 2 scanner labels CMP as `BUY_AT_CMP_NO_FOMO` (+3.58% above the 10-week EMA and RSI 57.68), we override and reject it for two decisive reasons. First, the S&P 500 is in a 10-distribution-day Downtrend (38.8% above 50-DMA; 3 of 11 sectors above 50-DMA), where low-beta leaders frequently suffer air-pocket resets. Second, Chapter 7 proved that probability-weighted EV ($373.00) yields just 0.04:1 R:R at CMP (0.42:1 Base) and only 1.18:1 R:R at the $355.00 50-day SMA shelf against the $339.73 snapshot stop reference.

Because the 50-day SMA shelf ($348.00–$355.00) itself fails our 1.50:1 asymmetry hurdle on reconciled EV, we do not stage resting buy bids there. Instead, we assign REJECTED (TIER_0) and restrict our monitor-only conditional re-open watch strictly below $330.00–$345.00 (bridging Pivot S1 at $336.41 and our $323.54–$336.96 sensitivity floor). Re-opening requires S&P 500 exit from Downtrend, a confirmed 4H/daily upward turn, and NA Commercial long-tail adverse PPD stabilizing below $150M–$192M/quarter, with a fresh stop recalculated after base repair.

Our November 20 options scan (`options_US_batch5.json`) confirms NO_OPTIONS_EDGE. No clean call-spread strikes exist above $305 on the February 19, 2027 expiration. With 1.81% daily ATR and thin strike liquidity, we skip all option structures and hold 100% cash.

book_paragraphs: Open the price chart for November 20, 2026, and the tension between Chubb's longer-term chart and the broader market's deterioration is unmistakable. The S&P 500 sits in a confirmed Downtrend with 10 institutional distribution days over 25 sessions, just 38.8% of stocks above their 50-day moving averages, and only 3 of 11 sectors holding trend. Chubb closed at $371.63—still above its 10-week EMA ($358.80), 50-day SMA ($352.46), and 30-week SMA ($343.09).

Both our daily market-facts ledger and TradingView snapshot tag Chubb as Stage 2, and the automated scanner marks CMP as non-extended. Yet looking closer at the tape reveals why blind scanner green lights trap disciplined capital. On the 4-hour chart, Chubb is stalled beneath its 4H 20-EMA ($371.81) with intraday_4h_turn equal to false and a 51.79 RSI, while the stock itself has absorbed 5 distribution days in 25 sessions.

More importantly, Chapter 7 showed that valuation math rejects both CMP and the 50-day moving average shelf. With Bear Justified P/B reconciled to $301.00 ($300.56 exact) and probability-weighted Expected Value at $373.00, buying at $371.63 offers 0.04-to-1 EV asymmetry (0.42-to-1 Base), and even waiting for $355.00 offers only 1.18-to-1 EV asymmetry against the $339.73 snapshot stop reference.

That is why we refuse to hide behind WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT. We assign REJECTED (TIER_0), skip options (NO_OPTIONS_EDGE above $305 strikes), and keep 100% of capital in USD cash—setting only a conditional re-open watch strictly below $330.00–$345.00 if the S&P 500 exits Downtrend, 4H/daily trend turns up, and casualty adverse PPD cools.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: A STAGE 2 LABEL NEVER OVERRULES FAILING MATH
book_callouts.text: An automated screen sees CB +3.58% above its 10-week EMA. It cannot see 10 S&P 500 distribution days, 5 CB distribution days, intraday_4h_turn = false, or 1.18:1 EV asymmetry at the 50-day SMA. Reject the setup and preserve cash.

book_subsections.title: Why 1W, 1D, and 4H Tape Friction Reinforces Valuation Rejection
paragraphs: Inspecting all three timeframes keeps portfolio risk honest. On the weekly chart, CB's 30-week SMA ($343.09) and 10-week EMA ($358.80) preserve a primary Stage 2 structure, yet five individual distribution days in 25 sessions warn that institutions are trimming into strength near $384.26.

On the 4-hour chart, price sits below the $371.81 4H 20-EMA with a 51.79 RSI and no reversal turn. In a 10-distribution-day S&P 500 Downtrend where defensive leaders routinely give back 8% to 12% during forced redemptions, setting resting bids at $355.00 for just 1.18:1 EV reward-to-risk is a poor wager.

Even the daily volume footprint confirms caution. Over the past 25 sessions, Chubb absorbed five distribution days while trading 1.47x 20-day average volume on November 20. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 logged 10 distribution days with only 38.8% of constituents above their 50-day moving averages and just 3 of 11 sectors holding trend. Fighting that market tape for 1.18-to-1 Expected Value asymmetry at $355.00 violates basic capital preservation.

book_subsections.title: The Conditional Re-Open Shelf Strictly Below $330.00–$345.00
paragraphs: Notice where technical support and fundamental stress tests converge: classic Pivot S1 sits at $336.41, the 200-day SMA sits at $338.77, and our Chapter 7 Justified P/B stress tests (12.5% ROE, +100 bps Ke, 50% AOCI persistence) cluster between $323.54 and $336.96. That is why any future re-evaluation belongs strictly below $330.00–$345.00—and only after S&P 500 exits Downtrend, 4H/daily trend turns up, and long-tail adverse PPD stabilizes below $150M–$192M per quarter.

book_subsections.title: Options Desk Check: Why We Pass on Call Spreads Today
paragraphs: Our live November 20 options chain scan across Chubb's listed expirations returned NO_OPTIONS_EDGE because no clean call-spread strikes exist above $305 on the February 19, 2027 expiration with acceptable liquidity and spread economics. Combining NO_OPTIONS_EDGE with a REJECTED (TIER_0) equity verdict keeps execution clean: 100% cash in USD Treasury bills.
